item.title: Shawnee wrestler Stetson Tucker takes second place at state
item.description: OKLAHOMA CITY – Shawnee High School had one state runner-up placer on the boys’ side and a third-place and a fourth-place finisher on the girls’ side to highlight efforts in the Class 5A State Wrestling Championships last Saturday at the new Fairgrounds Coliseum. In the boys’ division, Tucker Stetson had a second-place finish after going 3-1 in the event at 132 pounds.

item.title: The new face of Shawnee rock: Teenage powerhouse The Shawp re
item.description: SHAWNEE – The Shawp is returning to the historic Ritz Theater stage this Saturday, March 7, to prove they aren’t just a flash in the pan. The teenage blues outfit is set to headline their second appearance at the iconic venue, bringing a matured sound, new songs, and a rapidly growing fanbase with them.

item.title: Gardens of the Cross Timbers: The Fairy Horns are calling
item.description: If March comes in like a roaring lion, will it really leave like a gentle lamb? Far from sub-Sahara Africa where wild lions still live, the proverb goes back to 17th century England and became popular in farming areas. It may refer to the astrological Leo the Lion constellation in the sky, very visible this time of year.

item.title: Mabee-Gerrer Museum of Art announces winners of 6th Annual High School Juried Art Exhibition
item.description: SHAWNEE – The Mabee-Gerrer Museum of Art is proud to announce the winners of its 6th Annual High School Juried Art Exhibition, showcasing the outstanding talents of high school students from across Oklahoma. The exhibition, featuring an impressive array of 258 pieces of artwork in various mediums, will be on display through March 29.

item.title: Ever-shifting commerce develops Shawnee's landscape
item.description: Shawnee is no stranger to the ever-changing nature of its business district. Things come and go for a plethora of reasons.
